summary: Security questionnaire: clarify whether Redwood trains on customer prompts/data (approved wording + FAQ link)
description:
Issue summary:
Multiple enterprise prospects (latest: Summit Insurance) are asking a recurring questionnaire question:
- “Do you use customer data to train models?”
- “Do you fine-tune models using our prompts/responses?”
- “Is our content used to improve your services / shared across customers?”

Impact:
This question is gating security review completion. Field teams are currently answering inconsistently (some say “never retained” which conflicts with retention/logging nuance). Need a single approved response, including deployment-mode nuances (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and an internal pointer to evidence/FAQ.

Customer ask (verbatim from questionnaire):
“Confirm whether the provider uses Customer Content (including prompts, inputs, outputs, and metadata) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any AI/ML models. If yes, describe opt-out options and controls.”

Approved response (copy/paste; do not edit without Security/GRC review):
“Redwood Inference does not train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve our hosted or managed models using Customer Content (including prompts, inputs, outputs) by default. Customer Content is processed solely to provide the service (generate outputs, operate the platform, and provide support as requested). Any use of Customer Content for model training or evaluation would require the customer’s explicit opt-in and a separate written agreement.”

Important clarifications (include if asked):
- “Customer Content” definition: prompts/inputs and model outputs generated for the customer.
- Operational use: Redwood may process content for service delivery and troubleshooting when requested/authorized by the customer; access is role-based and logged.
- Telemetry/logging: platform logs (e.g., request metadata, performance metrics, error logs) may be collected for security, reliability, and billing. Retention varies by deployment mode and configuration; see the canonical retention overview.
- Shared responsibility: In Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, customers may control/host portions of logging and storage depending on architecture; Redwood’s control plane access and responsibilities are defined in the deployment design.

What NOT to say (common incorrect answers):
- Do not claim “we never store prompts” or “zero retention” unless the customer is on a specific configuration and Security has confirmed it in writing.
- Do not imply ISO 27001 certification in this answer.

Requested outcome:
1) Confirm the approved wording above is correct for use in questionnaires and RFPs.
2) Provide canonical link(s) to the updated Security FAQ section and internal ‘do/don’t say’ guidance.
3) If needed, add a snippet to the RFP response library under “Data Protection > Data Use / Model Training” (managed by GRC/Security Enablement).
comments: 2026-01-30 (Dev Patel): Logging this as a recurring blocker from the field. Summit Insurance security questionnaire due early next week; AE asking for a single approved paragraph. Similar question came up in Acme Health and Aurora Financial calls as well.

2026-01-31 (Olga Petrov): Confirming policy posture: we do NOT use customer prompts/outputs to train/fine-tune models by default. We need to keep wording aligned with retention language (avoid “never stored”). Recommend the approved block include “by default” + “explicit opt-in + separate written agreement.”

2026-02-01 (Marcus Lin): +1. Also add: access to customer content (when required for support) is limited and audited. Don’t over-promise on “no employee ever sees content” because support escalation can require customer authorization and time-bound access.

2026-02-02 (Naomi Feldman): Please ensure this answer does not imply any future roadmap. Approved phrasing: “does not … by default” and “any use … would require explicit opt-in and a separate written agreement.” That matches our current commitments.

2026-02-03 (Daniel Carter): I’m aligning this with the refreshed Security FAQ. Proposed canonical link for Sales/SEs: Confluence > Sales Enablement > Security FAQ (2026) > “Data use, model training, and customer content.” Once posted, please reference the page rather than rephrasing.

2026-02-05 (Dev Patel): Field request: can we include a one-liner for questionnaires that ask “is customer data shared across tenants?” Suggested addition (only if asked): “Customer Content is logically isolated by tenant; Redwood does not share Customer Content across customers.” Please confirm if OK to include.

2026-02-06 (Marcus Lin): OK to include “not shared across customers” in this context, but keep it scoped to content (not logs/metadata), and avoid technical claims like “physically air-gapped” unless it’s Dedicated/Private-specific and confirmed in the deployment design.
resolution: Provided approved questionnaire wording for “no training on customer data by default” with opt-in + separate written agreement caveat, plus guidance on what not to say. Linked Sales/SEs to the canonical Security FAQ section and internal do/don’t-say guidance. Confirmed optional add-on line for “not shared across customers” with scoping caveats.
resolution_notes: Action for field: use the ‘Approved response’ paragraph verbatim in questionnaires. If a customer presses on retention/logging, point them to the customer-facing retention overview and offer a security review call. Do not add claims about ‘zero retention’ or ‘no employee access’ without Security confirmation for the specific deployment/config.
